questionText:
Consider the canonical $LR(0)$ parsing of the grammar below using terminals $\{a, b, c\}$ and non-terminals $\{A, B, C, S\}$ with $S$ as the start symbol.

$$S \rightarrow ACB$$
$$A \rightarrow aA \mid \epsilon$$
$$C \rightarrow cC \mid \epsilon$$
$$B \rightarrow bB \mid b$$

Which one of the following options gives the number of shift-reduce conflicts that will occur in the $LR(0)$ ACTION table?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Augmented Grammar:
$$S' \rightarrow S$$
$$S \rightarrow ACB$$
$$A \rightarrow aA \mid \epsilon$$
$$C \rightarrow cC \mid \epsilon$$
$$B \rightarrow bB \mid b$$

2. Constructing $LR(0)$ States and Identifying Conflicts:
In an $LR(0)$ ACTION table, a shift-reduce conflict occurs in a cell $(\text{State}, \text{Terminal})$ if the state has a shift transition on that terminal and also contains a reduce item (which places a reduce action across all terminal columns).

• State 1 ($I_0$): $\{S' \rightarrow \cdot S, S \rightarrow \cdot ACB, A \rightarrow \cdot aA, A \rightarrow \cdot\}$
Shift on '$a$' and Reduce $A \rightarrow \epsilon$ on '$a$' (1st Conflict).

• State 2 ($I_3$): $\{A \rightarrow a \cdot A, A \rightarrow \cdot aA, A \rightarrow \cdot\}$
Shift on '$a$' and Reduce $A \rightarrow \epsilon$ on '$a$' (2nd Conflict).

• State 3 ($I_2$): $\{S \rightarrow A \cdot CB, C \rightarrow \cdot cC, C \rightarrow \cdot\}$
Shift on '$c$' and Reduce $C \rightarrow \epsilon$ on '$c$' (3rd Conflict).

• State 4 ($I_5$): $\{C \rightarrow c \cdot C, C \rightarrow \cdot cC, C \rightarrow \cdot\}$
Shift on '$c$' and Reduce $C \rightarrow \epsilon$ on '$c$' (4th Conflict).

• State 5 ($I_8$): $\{B \rightarrow b \cdot B, B \rightarrow b \cdot, B \rightarrow \cdot bB, B \rightarrow \cdot b\}$
Shift on '$b$' and Reduce $B \rightarrow b$ on '$b$' (5th Conflict).

Thus, there are exactly 5 shift-reduce conflicts in total.

Hence, Option (D) is the correct answer.
